html:
Hello

Here is a wide-field image of the southern part of the constellation Orion. This part of the sky holds some of the most beautiful objects in the celestial vault.

Among them,
  • the Orion Nebula (Messier 42), visible in the center of the photo, a little below the middle.
  • Messier 43, a nebula just north of Messier 42.
  • The Running Man Nebula (NGC 1973/5/7).
  • the Horsehead Nebula (IC 434). Small red cloud in the center left.
  • the Flame Nebula (NGC 2024).
  • Orion's Belt. The three stars in the center of the photo
  • Barnard's Loop. The red cloud that runs through the photo from north to south on the left side.
  • the Witch Head Nebula. Hard to see in the lower right corner of the image


Technical details:
Date: 2009-10-17
Temperature: 0 to -2 degrees celsius.
Telescope: Canon 50 mm f1.4 lens @ f4.0
Sensor: Canon 40D unfiltered
Filter: IDAS-LPS (to counter light pollution)
Mount: LX200 10" f 6.3 classic
Guiding: QHY5 and PHD

9 frames of 300 seconds (1 rejected because of the factory smoke), 10 darks, 10 flats
Calibrated and stacked in Nebulosity
Processing in photoshop
